newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Macedonia, Croatia sign free trade agreement.
newsitem.headline: Macedonia, Croatia sign free trade agreement.

text.p: Macedonia and Croatia signed an agreement on free trade here on Friday in order to create conditions for the establishment of a free trade zone by January 2000.
"I am convinced this will help to further improve our economic cooperation," visiting Croatian Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa told Croatian state news agency HINA. No details of the deal were given.
Macedonian Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski said "there are no disputed quesitons between the two countries."
Members of the chambers of commerce of the two former Yugoslav republics said a joint chamber would soon be established.
Before the break-up of former Yugoslavia, the total annual exchange between Macedonia and Croatia was $800 million, but has dwindled to under $170 million.
The two countries now plan to intensify exchange of agricultural, food and metal industry products, HINA said.
Croatia plans to sign a similar deal with its northern neighbour Slovenia and other central European countries, said Matesa.
